taskNaming.summary: Naming task titles automatically: what it spends, which stages it runs at, and how often people rename what it wrote

kpi.visitorsNote: Counted per person per day: reading the docs three times in one day is one visitor, and the same browser on another day is another one.
kpi.loggedInNote: Visitors carrying an account. The rest are anonymous readers, who keep only a random id generated at that moment — the platform does not know who they are.
kpi.askersNote: People who asked at least once in the window. The denominator is signed-in visitors: asking requires signing in, and counting against everyone who read the docs would make this share fall whenever a signed-out reader arrived.
kpi.questionsNote: Every question received in the window; the same question asked three times counts three times.
kpi.answerRateNote: Answered questions as a share of all of them. The rest split into "no answer found" and "failed", listed separately below.
kpi.costNote: Estimated from the recorded tokens at the gateway's price list, **not a bill figure**: this virtual key cannot read spend for a window. {tokens} tokens carry no price there and are left out.
kpi.costUnknownNote: The gateway's price list could not be read, so this figure is unknown — it is not drawn as 0, because 0 reads as "free".

trend.title: Day by day
trend.note: Three lines, three questions: how many came, how many of them asked, and how many questions were asked. A day with nothing is drawn as 0 rather than a gap — a gap reads as "not measured".

tokens.title: Tokens per question
tokens.note: Per question, not per day: a day's total is skewed by one long conversation. Only questions whose tokens were recorded are counted.
tokens.caption: {n} questions

histogram.title: Token distribution
histogram.note: Each bar is how many questions fall in that range. Two usages with the same average and different shapes (everyone asks 3,000 against nine in ten asking 300) are told apart here.

latency.title: How long an answer takes
latency.note: From receiving the question to finishing the answer. The median is the usual speed; p90 is how slow it gets — that is the number readers complain about.
latency.caption: {n} answers

outcomes.title: How answers ended
outcomes.note: The three add up to every question in the window. The two below "answered" are worth keeping apart: a missing answer is the docs' problem, a failure is the platform's.

unanswered.title: Questions it could not answer
unanswered.note: Grouped by the question text, most-asked first, fifty rows at most. **There is no, and never will be, a "who asked" column**: this is a list for whoever writes the docs, not a user report.
unanswered.empty: Nothing went unanswered in this window.

kpi.callsNote: Requests on the gateway's dedicated naming key. Naming runs in the background, outside any run someone started, so these calls count against no project's usage.
kpi.successRateNote: The gateway's own reading: the request reached the model and came back. A truncated answer, or one wrapped in broken JSON, is still a success there — those are only written to the log, which is why this page has no "naming success rate".
kpi.tokensNote: What naming sends in and writes back. Both its prompt and its answer are short, so this number is mainly here to catch the model starting to ramble.
kpi.costNote: The gateway's own books, not an estimate. The figure above is this window's; the key line is what the gateway keeps for that key, over its own budget period — not the same window.
kpi.costUnknownNote: The gateway could not be read, so this figure is unknown — it is not drawn as 0, because 0 reads as "costs nothing".
kpi.costNoKeyNote: The gateway answered, but has no dedicated naming key — naming never minted one, or its alias changed. This figure is unknown: it is not drawn as 0, because 0 says "the key is there and spent nothing this window".
kpi.renamesNote: A row is written only when the title actually changes, so this counts renames, not looks.
kpi.overriddenNote: The denominator is tasks automatically named within the window, including titles the AI teammate proposed. The numerator is those later renamed by a person within the same window. Automatic titles from before the window are excluded; this is not a lifetime retention rate.

trend.title: Titles written per day
trend.note: Two lines for two things: what the platform renamed, and what people renamed. A day with no titles is drawn as 0 rather than a gap — a gap reads as "not measured".

stages.title: Which stage naming ran at
stages.note: After the first name comes calibration, a second look at the task's first real message, and follow, which only fires when the task changes direction. The split says when the model usually steps in.
stages.caption: {n} automatic renames
stages.name: First name

person.title: What people changed
person.note: Titles people gave tasks themselves. Once a person renames a task, the platform leaves that name alone.
person.caption: {n} renames by people

kpi.checksSplit: {allowed} taken directly, {asked} confirmed by the user
kpi.checksNote: Each action others can see is checked once before Cheese takes it for the user
kpi.askedNote: Actions that need confirmation appear as cards in the panel; a high share means the check is strict
kpi.costNote: Paid by the platform, not from personal credits
kpi.gateCacheNote: Share of the checks' prompts served from the model provider's cache
kpi.answerCacheNote: Share of each answer's model-call prompts served from the model provider's cache
kpi.latencyNote: Only checks that called the model; those settled by the user's settings are not counted

trend.title: Authorization checks per day
trend.note: The dashed line is those needing the user's confirmation

stages.title: How it was decided
stages.note: User settings and low-risk actions are decided without the model; a quick check gives only a verdict, and one that does not pass is reviewed again
stages.asked:rule: Confirmed per the user's settings or a fixed rule

kinds.title: By action type
kinds.note: How often each action type was taken directly or confirmed by the user
